title: Ben Webster resents Lester Young's arrival
summary: Ben Webster disliked Lester Young's showmanship and walk up Seventh Avenue and threatened him; they discuss Lester's manner.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: Well, no, I guess -- I guess from
what you say then that Chu actually does not follow you and all of them. I mean some of those Texas people must have been before him.
Let me see now. When Earl Hines came here, Bud Johnson was with Earl Hines' band, and—
Well, I mean Bud had been gone a long time before he got with Earl (unintelligible).
Yeah, I think Chu was before them fellows.

Yeah, because now when Lester came in, Lester came in -- Lester was supposed to go with Fletcher, and then Ben went with Fletcher. Ben didn't have -- those guys was funny -- [Bird] (unintelligible) didn't impress me nothing. Lester -- kind of like a showmanship, you know -- and Lester walk up, set his horn on his shoulder, you know, (unintelligible). So Ben came and said to me, said, look at that son of a bitch over there, going up Seventh Avenue with that horn on his --
Who said this to you, Ben --
Ben Webster. Ben didn't like him.
See, what happened, before Hawk came

back from Europe, Lester was here. See, he came here to join Fletcher's band. He came and so did Ben. Ben came in earlier than Lester. And everybody was talking about this thing, you know, and naturally Lester take it to heart and Ben --and Ben couldn't take it. Hap, I ought to go over there and punch that so and so and so on in the mouth. Look at that.
I said, Ben, let him alone. Nothing you can do with him.
Do you think it had anything to do with the fact that Lester's sort of manner was a bit effeminate or anything?
Well, you know, he carried that way, but he actually wasn't that [sissy,] was he?
No, I know he wasn't. But I mean some people might have thought he was queer.
